title: RemoteFunction:InvokeClient()
summary: Server asks ONE client a question and yields for the answer. Risky: the client may be slow, broken, or malicious — always use the timeout parameter and never base security on the reply.

parameters.name: timeoutSeconds
parameters.description: Optional timeout — errors if the client doesn't answer in time. STRONGLY recommended.

reference.returns: Whatever the client's OnClientInvoke returns — never trust it for authoritative logic.

details.heading: Failure modes
details.body: If the client has no OnClientInvoke set, errors, or never returns, the invoke errors/times out. pcall it.

explanation.whatItIs: The rare reverse question: server → client with an expected answer.
explanation.whyItExists: Occasionally the server needs client-side knowledge (e.g., 'which slot did you select?' after a client menu) — but design hard to avoid needing it.
whenToUse: Genuinely client-known facts needed synchronously, with a timeout
Legacy patterns; new designs usually invert the flow (client fires first)
whenNotToUse: Anything frequent — the server yielding on clients serializes badly
If the client could initiate instead — invert the flow and use FireServer
tips: ALWAYS pass a timeout and pcall
Treat timeout/no-response as the safe default
Validate the reply like any client data
commonMistakes: No timeout → server threads hanging on unresponsive clients
InvokeClient-ing inside OnServerInvoke for the same player → deadlock

examples.title: Asking with a timeout
examples.code:
-- Client sets up the answerer:
rf.OnClientInvoke = function(question)
    if question == "SelectedSlot" then
        return currentSlot
    end
end

-- Server asks, safely:
local ok, answer = pcall(function()
    return rf:InvokeClient(player, 5, "SelectedSlot")
end)
local slot = (ok and typeof(answer) == "number") and answer or 1   -- safe default
